cold_email.subject: Interest in Full Time Educator / POLARIS FASHION PLACE — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear lululemon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Full Time Educator / POLARIS FASHION PLACE opportunity with lululemon at lululemon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Assistant I - CWID — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear The Henry M. Jackson Foundation for the Advancement of Military Medicine Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Assistant I - CWID opportunity with The Henry M. Jackson Foundation for the Advancement of Military Medicine at The Henry M. Jackson Foundation for the Advancement of Military Medicine.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Pre-ETS Instructor - Canton NY — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Public Consulting Group Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Pre-ETS Instructor - Canton NY opportunity with Public Consulting Group at Public Consulting Group.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Intellectual Disability - Program Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Keystone Human Services Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Intellectual Disability - Program Coordinator opportunity with Keystone Human Services at Keystone Human Services.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Operations Associate, University Hills, #478 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Gopuff Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Operations Associate, University Hills, #478 opportunity with Gopuff at Gopuff.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Operations Associate, University Park, #602 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Gopuff Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Operations Associate, University Park, #602 opportunity with Gopuff at Gopuff.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,

cold_email.subject: Interest in Youth Development Counselor (Evening/Overnight Shifts) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Good Shepherd Services Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Youth Development Counselor (Evening/Overnight Shifts) opportunity with Good Shepherd Services at Good Shepherd Services.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Youth Development Counselor (Full-Time): Green House Residential Program — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Good Shepherd Services Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Youth Development Counselor (Full-Time): Green House Residential Program opportunity with Good Shepherd Services at Good Shepherd Services.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Program Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Charles R. Drew University of Medicine and Science Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Program Coordinator opportunity with Charles R. Drew University of Medicine and Science at Charles R. Drew University of Medicine and Science.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Professional – Erik Hurst and Chang-Tai Hsieh (Full-Time, Benefits Eligible) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Becker Friedman Institute for Economics Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Professional – Erik Hurst and Chang-Tai Hsieh (Full-Time, Benefits Eligible) opportunity with Becker Friedman Institute for Economics at Becker Friedman Institute for Economics.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Project Coordinator (4 year term) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Northwestern University Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Project Coordinator (4 year term) opportunity with Northwestern University at Northwestern University.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Home Health Physical Therapist — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear ProSource Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Home Health Physical Therapist opportunity with ProSource at ProSource.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Swim Instructor — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear British Swim School Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Swim Instructor opportunity with British Swim School at British Swim School.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Analytics Engineer II, Commercialization
jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. Position Summary The Commercial Data & AI HYD team is seeking an Analytics Engineer II to build and own the analytics-layer transformations that connect curated data to the dashboards, self-service BI, and advanced analytics used across the business. This role operates as part of a deployed engineering model, working closely with an assigned Commercial business domain (e.g., Sales, Marketing, Market Access, or Medical Affairs) to keep the analytics layer aligned with how that part of the business actually operates. The successful candidate will analyze business requirements and build, test, and integrate the application components, tools, and utilities that support commercial reporting and analytics consumption, while owning the transformation logic, dimensional models, and metrics definitions for assigned data domains on the Databricks Lakehouse. This role offers the opportunity to build strong technical depth in analytics engineering on Databricks, with growth potential toward more senior data modeling and solution architecture responsibilities. Key Responsibilities Design, build, and own analytics-layer transformations, semantic models, and metrics for assigned data domains, turning curated data into trusted, self-serve analytics products on Databricks. Analyze business requirements and build, test, and integrate the application components, tools, and utilities that support commercial reporting and analytics consumption. Build analytics-ready data models — star/snowflake schemas, conformed dimensions, fact tables — that turn commercial business logic into consistent, reusable structures. Apply performance and cost-optimization practices for Databricks workloads within assigned pipelines, including cluster configuration and Delta Lake optimization (Z-ordering, partitioning, OPTIMIZE/VACUUM). Develop and maintain SQL- and Python-based transformation logic that integrates structured and semi-structured commercial datasets (sales, claims, patient, payer, HUB, specialty pharmacy). Implement data quality checks, validation routines, and reconciliation logic for assigned datasets, following established testing and documentation standards. Document data products, metric definitions, lineage, and known limitations in accordance with internal governance standards. Work as part of a deployed engineering team embedded with an assigned Commercial business domain, partnering with analysts, BI developers, and business stakeholders to support dashboard and reporting use cases. Apply data governance standards and access controls for sensitive and regulated data, including PII/PHI awareness. Provide guidance to Analytics Engineer I team members on data modeling and engineering best practices. Skills & Competencies Strong proficiency in SQL and Python for analytics transformations, data modeling, and validation. Hands-on experience with Databricks (notebooks, jobs/workflows) and working knowledge of Delta Lake concepts (ACID tables, Z-ordering, partitioning). Solid experience with dimensional data modeling — star/snowflake schemas, conformed dimensions, fact tables, SCD handling. Familiarity with lakehouse/medallion architecture concepts (bronze/silver/gold layers). Working knowledge of cloud data engineering fundamentals (e.g., AWS storage, compute, and IAM concepts). Experience with data quality practices, including profiling, validation, and reconciliation. Working knowledge of software engineering practices including Git/version control, code reviews, and CI/CD. Familiarity with BI/visualization tools (Tableau, Power BI) and a clear sense of what makes a dataset genuinely self-service. Strong problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to work independently on well-defined analytics domains. Comfort working as part of a deployed team embedded within a business domain, adapting to domain-specific priorities. We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway. How We Work Where you work matters – because collaboration, innovation and patient impact happen in many settings. Our roles are structured across four work models: site-essential, site-by-design, field-based and remote-by-design. The model assigned to this role is based on its core responsibilities. jobs.title: Sr Systems Test Engineer
jobs.description: What if the work you did every day could impact the lives of people you know? Or all of humanity? At Illumina, we are expanding access to genomic technology to realize health equity for billions of people around the world. Our efforts enable life-changing discoveries that are transforming human health through the early detection and diagnosis of diseases and new treatment options for patients. Working at Illumina means being part of something bigger than yourself. Every person, in every role, has the opportunity to make a difference. Surrounded by extraordinary people, inspiring leaders, and world changing projects, you will do more and become more than you ever thought possible. Summary The Senior Systems Test Engineer will lead system-level engineering verification activities for complex sequencing platforms from early development through product launch. This role is responsible for developing verification strategies, executing system and thermal performance testing, identifying technical risks, and ensuring products meet performance, reliability, and quality objectives. The position partners closely with cross-functional engineering teams to evaluate integrated system behavior, drive data-based decisions, and establish verification best practices across product development programs. Responsibilities Lead system-level engineering verification and test activities for next-generation sequencing platforms from development through product launch. Develop verification strategies, test plans, methodologies, and execution approaches aligned with product requirements and risk profiles. Design and execute testing to evaluate system performance, reliability, and robustness across normal, boundary, stress, fault, and worst-case conditions. Lead characterization and verification of thermal management and temperature-control systems, including performance, stability, and operating margin assessments. Conduct data-driven investigations using statistical analysis, design of experiments (DOE), and root cause analysis to identify and resolve technical issues. Partner with Systems, Hardware, Software, Controls, Quality, Manufacturing, and Operations teams to define requirements, troubleshoot issues, and drive product readiness. Drive continuous improvement through test automation, standardized methodologies, reusable test infrastructure, and data analytics. Communicate test results, technical risks, and recommendations to stakeholders and leadership, while providing technical mentorship and guidance to engineering teams. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Controls Engineering, or a related technical discipline. Typically requires a minimum of 5 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree; or 3 years and a Master's degree; or a PhD without experience; or equivalent work experience. Experience developing and executing system-level verification and validation strategies for complex systems. Experience with engineering verification, requirements traceability, test planning, and risk-based testing methodologies. Experience testing thermal management systems, including TEC/Peltier-based control systems or comparable temperature-control technologies. Experience with DOE, statistical analysis, margin characterization, troubleshooting, and root cause analysis. Experience developing test methods, fixtures, instrumentation, and data analysis approaches for complex systems. Proven ability to work effectively across multiple engineering disciplines and influence technical decisions without direct authority. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical findings to a variety of audiences. Preferred Qualifications Master's degree in a relevant engineering discipline. Experience with DNA sequencing systems or other high-throughput analytical or life science instrumentation. Familiarity with next-generation sequencing (NGS) platforms, sequencing workflows, or related technologies. Experience with thermal control of flow cells, reagent systems, or other precision temperature-controlled processes. Experience developing automated test systems and analysis tools using Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, or similar platforms. Experience with Jira, requirements management tools, test management systems, and engineering data platforms. Experience with reliability engineering, accelerated life testing, environmental testing, and failure analysis. Familiarity with Design Controls, Design Verification processes, and regulated product development environments. Experience leading technical initiatives, driving cross-functional projects, or mentoring engineers. cold_email.subject: Interest in Sr Systems Test Engineer — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Illumina Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Sr Systems Test Engineer opportunity with Illumina at Illumina.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Scientist 3 - Translational Medicine
jobs.description: We advance science so that we all have more time with the people we love. Genentech's Translational Medicine OMNI (TM OMNI) team supports the entire R&D portfolio of novel therapies across Ophthalmology, Metabolism, Neuroscience, Immunology, and Infectious Diseases. We develop and implement cutting-edge translational research and biomarker strategies to identify complex disease pathways, validate mechanisms of action, and accelerate clinical trial success. Scientists within our department leverage deep clinical insights to drive next-generation target identification and champion end-to-end biomarker execution, from initial discovery to final data interpretation. Opportunity: We are seeking a talented and highly motivated Scientist 3 to join Genentech’s Translational Medicine (TM) team on-site at our South San Francisco campus. In this role, you will partner with cross-functional R&D teams to drive translational research for next-generation therapeutic targets and provide critical biomarker support for glaucoma neuroprotection programs throughout the drug development lifecycle. This position uniquely bridges data science and the wet lab, requiring a blend of computational skills to interpret high-dimensional datasets and bench-level expertise to design and execute validation experiments. This is a hands-on, high-impact opportunity for a scientist eager to apply their training to drive foundational science and establish a new disease area at Genentech, navigating the complexities of ophthalmic drug development within a deeply collaborative environment. As an integral member of our dynamic team, you will: Analyze high-dimensional datasets (e.g., proteomics, transcriptomics) generated from clinical and preclinical samples to discover novel therapeutic targets and candidate biomarkers. Design and execute experiments using disease-relevant in vitro human cell models to translate data-driven insights into functional biology. Lead and coordinate exploratory clinical studies in partnership with internal and external collaborators to advance translational research and discover clinical biomarkers. Collaborate closely with cross-functional R&D partners, including Research Biology, Computational Sciences, Tissue Genomics & Proteomics, Biostatistics, Clinical Pharmacology, and Bioanalytical Sciences. Develop and qualify custom assays (e.g., Simoa, NULISA) for biomarkers of interest, moving beyond standard commercial kits to build bespoke solutions for pipeline programs. Communicate insights effectively across the organization and the broader scientific community through high-quality reports, presentations, and peer-reviewed publications. Who You Are: The ideal candidate will bring: A PhD in Biological Sciences (including neuroscience, immunology, cell biology, or a related field) with 0–4 years of relevant post-graduate experience. Exceptional candidates without a PhD but with an equivalent track record of rigorous scientific experience are also encouraged to apply. While clinical or translational experience in retinal biology is preferred, it is not required. We welcome applicants with broad biological expertise who are eager to apply their skills to a new disease area. A proven track record of executing both wet-lab experiments and bioinformatic analyses to answer complex biological questions, as demonstrated through a strong peer-reviewed publication record. Deep technical wet-lab expertise in preclinical/clinical sample analysis and molecular biology techniques (including cell culture, ELISA, qPCR, and NGS/transcriptomics). Computational proficiency with hands-on experience programming in R or Python to apply biostatistical and bioinformatics methods to high-dimensional datasets. Demonstrated scientific independence, outstanding organizational and teamwork skills, scientific curiosity, and exceptional communication abilities with a clear passion for translating science into life-changing therapies. Relocation benefits are not available for this posting. The expected salary range for this position based on the primary location of California is $100,400 -186,400. Actual pay will be determined based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other job-related factors permitted by law. A discretionary annual bonus may be available based on individual and Company performance. This position also qualifies for the benefits detailed at the link provided below. Benefits Genentech is an equal opportunity employer. It is our policy and practice to employ, promote, and otherwise treat any and all employees and applicants on the basis of merit, qualifications, and competence. The company's policy prohibits unlawful discrimination, including but not limited to, discrimination on the basis of Protected Veteran status, individuals with disabilities status, and consistent with all federal, state, or local laws. If you have a disability and need an accommodation in relation to the online application process, please contact us by completing this form Accommodations for Applicants .

cold_email.subject: Interest in Scientist 3 - Translational Medicine — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Genentech / Roche Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Scientist 3 - Translational Medicine opportunity with Genentech / Roche at Genentech / Roche.

I am especially interested in the lab's combination of neurotechnology, quantitative biology, and questions about brain-wide computation. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background spans biology, scientific programming, and reproducible data pipelines, and I am eager to apply that mix in a neuroscience setting.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Data Scientist (Open Level)
jobs.description: ABOUT FORMATION BIO Formation Bio is a tech and AI driven pharma company differentiated by radically more efficient drug development. Advancements in AI and drug discovery are creating more candidate drugs than the industry can progress because of the high cost and time of clinical trials. Recognizing that this development bottleneck may ultimately limit the number of new medicines that can reach patients, Formation Bio, founded in 2016 as TrialSpark Inc., has built technology platforms, processes, and capabilities to accelerate all aspects of drug development and clinical trials. Formation Bio partners, acquires, or in-licenses drugs from pharma companies, research organizations, and biotechs to develop programs past clinical proof of concept and beyond, ultimately helping to bring new medicines to patients. The company is backed by investors across pharma and tech, including a16z, Sequoia, Sanofi, Thrive Capital, John Doerr, Spark Capital, SV Angel Growth, and others. You can read more at the following links: - Our Vision for AI in Pharma https://www.formation.bio/blog/our-vision-for-ai-in-pharma - Our Current Drug Portfolio https://www.formation.bio/licensing-and-pipeline - Our Technology & Platform https://www.formation.bio/technology At Formation Bio, our values are the driving force behind our mission to revolutionize the pharma industry. Every team and individual at the company shares these same values, and every team and individual plays a key part in our mission to bring new treatments to patients faster and more efficiently. About the Position As a Data Scientist at Formation Bio, you will be at the forefront of revolutionizing drug development through AI and advanced analytics. In this role, you'll lead crucial initiatives that directly impact our drug development portfolio, from developing sophisticated models for patient selection to creating AI-powered solutions for clinical trial optimization. You'll work at the intersection of computational biology, machine learning, and drug development, collaborating with cross-functional teams to translate complex biological data into actionable insights. This position offers a unique opportunity to shape the future of pharmaceutical development by leveraging cutting-edge AI technologies while making a meaningful impact on patient lives. Responsibilities - Lead and execute complex data science projects that directly advance our drug development portfolio - Develop and implement sophisticated models for therapeutic hypothesis evaluation, including patient stratification and biomarker identification - Design and create AI models for modernizing clinical trial evaluations, including surrogate endpoints - Aid in the development and training of AI agents to automate and optimize biomedical workflows - Collaborate cross-functionally with clinical, technical, and research teams - Present complex analytical findings to senior stakeholders, including executive leadership About You Required Qualifications - PhD in computational sciences or life sciences - 3-5+ years of post-academic experience in life sciences (biotech, pharma, consulting) - Strong programming skills, particularly in Python - Extensive experience in multi-modal bioinformatics analysis Preferred Qualifications - Proven expertise in cloud computing environments, including proficiency with tabular and/or graph databases - Strong background in machine learning and deep learning, particularly in biological applications - Experience with large language models (LLM) - Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with engineering teams on production systems - Strong communication skills with proven ability to present complex technical findings to senior stakeholders Total Compensation Range: $161,500 - $267,000 Compensation Individual compensation is determined by several factors, including role scope, geographic location, and skills & experience. Applicants from the Research Triangle (NC) and San Francisco Bay Area may also be considered. Please apply only if you reside in these locations or are willing to relocate. Equal Opportunity Formation Bio is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome candidates from all backgrounds. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding, and related medical conditions), gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. We've seen a rise in recruiting impersonation scams across the industry, where fake profiles pose as recruiters aiming to trick candidates into sharing personal and financial information through illegitimate interviews and job offers. All legitimate recruiting communications from Formation Bio will come from a @formation.bio http://formation.bio email address. If you receive outreach from someone claiming to work at Formation Bio through any other domain or channel, please disregard it and do not share any personal information.

jobs.title: Scientist 3, Lung Biology & Inflammation
jobs.description: Why Genentech We’re passionate about delivering on Our Promise to improve the lives of patients and create healthier communities for all. We foster a culture of inclusivity, integrity and creativity while boldly pursuing answers to the world’s most complex health challenges and transforming society. The Opportunity The Department of Immunology at Genentech is seeking a driven Scientist with deep expertise in lung biology and immunology to uncover novel therapeutic targets for respiratory diseases. In this role, you will lead research projects investigating the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the lung's response to injury, chronic inflammation, and repair. Lead projects investigating cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying lung injury, chronic inflammation, and tissue repair. Advance novel research-stage programs into early clinical development by generating robust proof-of-concept data. Utilize state-of-the-art technologies, including in vitro and in vivo models, to evaluate novel molecules and targeted delivery systems. Dissect the pathogenesis of inflammatory lung diseases and identify the mechanism of action (MOA) of breakthrough therapies. Drive pipeline research while actively exploring new biologies and pathways for target discovery. Facilitate fruitful, open collaborations across immunology, human genetics, biomarker discovery, and early clinical development. Present research findings effectively at intra- and inter-departmental scientific meetings. Who you are PhD in immunology, stem cell biology, molecular biology, biochemistry, or a related field, with a demonstrated record of high-quality publications. Deep understanding of lung biology, particularly in chronic respiratory diseases, tissue remodeling/regeneration, or host-microbe interactions. Strong hands-on expertise in molecular biology, including cellular transfections, gene expression profiling, precision genome editing, and targeted RNA delivery technologies. Hands-on experience with primary cell isolation from human or mouse tissues, in vitro immunological assays, and multi-dimensional flow cytometry. Track record of independently designing, executing, troubleshooting, and interpreting complex experiments leading to first-author publication(s) in top-tier journals. Preferred Proven experience with complex in vitro systems, including airway/alveolar organoids, air-liquid interface (ALI) 3D cultures, or organ-on-a-chip technologies. jobs.title: Research Scientist, Life Sciences (Computational Chemistry)
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic's Life Sciences team is building a research group focused on biological discoveries by combining AI with hands-on biological research. We're seeking a research scientist who combines deep chemistry knowledge with machine learning expertise to join the team. Our goal is to speed up progress in the life sciences by an order of magnitude, and this role puts that mission into practice. You'll be a computational chemist who knows reactions, synthesis, and medicinal chemistry in depth and has hands-on experience training and evaluating machine learning models. Above all, you'll build the reinforcement learning environments, datasets, and evaluations that teach Claude chemistry. Working alongside our bench chemists and AI researchers, you'll turn real chemistry problems and experimental data into training tasks and measure whether the models get better at them. This role is fully on-site in the San Francisco Bay Area. Key responsibilities Design and build reinforcement learning environments for chemistry end to end, including task design, data curation, automated grading, and checks against shortcuts and data leakage Design and source new experimental datasets, environments, and evaluations with our bench chemists, and external research and academic partners Develop evaluations that measure model performance on real chemistry tasks, such as reaction outcome prediction, synthesis planning, structure elucidation, and compound design, and feed results back to research teams Run and analyze training experiments with AI research teams, diagnose where models fail at chemistry, and prioritize what to build next Ensure datasets and environments are high quality and well documented, including sources, train and test splits, and failure modes Communicate findings clearly to chemistry, AI research, and life sciences audiences Minimum qualifications PhD in chemistry, computational chemistry, or a related field Deep knowledge of organic and medicinal chemistry, including reactions, synthesis, and SAR, with experimental data as your ground truth Strong Python skills and solid machine learning fundamentals, with hands-on experience training and evaluating models Comfort navigating ambiguity and defining problems in a rapidly evolving research environment Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across cross-functional teams, with strong written and verbal communication skills Preferred qualifications Experience with reinforcement learning, large language models, or building evaluations and benchmarks Track record of supporting drug discovery programs alongside medicinal and synthetic chemists Experience curating chemistry datasets from the literature, patents, or lab notebooks, including reaction, ADMET, and spectroscopic data Cheminformatics and molecular modeling skills, for example RDKit, docking, free energy calculations, or quantum chemistry Hands-on synthetic or medicinal chemistry experience at the bench Publications, patents, or open-source software demonstrating scientific impact The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $300,000 — $320,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Administrative Coordinator opportunity with Amgen at Amgen.

Formation Bio partners, acquires, or in-licenses drugs from pharma companies, research organizations, and biotechs to develop programs past clinical proof of concept and beyond, ultimately helping to bring new medicines to patients. About the Position As a Senior Data Scientist - Medical Imaging at Formation Bio, you will lead our efforts to integrate advanced imaging analytics and AI into our drug development pipeline. In this role, you'll pioneer the application of computer vision and deep learning to medical imaging data (MRI, X-ray, CT, PET) to accelerate clinical trials and improve patient outcomes. You'll develop state-of-the-art models for automated image analysis, disease progression monitoring, and treatment response assessment. Working closely with clinical teams, radiologists, and drug development experts, you'll translate complex imaging data into actionable insights that drive key decisions across our portfolio. This position offers a unique opportunity to revolutionize how medical imaging is leveraged in pharmaceutical development while directly impacting patient care. Responsibilities - Lead the development of advanced deep learning models for medical image analysis, focusing on MRI and X-ray modalities for clinical trial applications - Design and implement automated image processing pipelines for disease detection, segmentation, and quantification across multiple therapeutic areas - Create innovative approaches for longitudinal image analysis to track disease progression and treatment efficacy in clinical trials, incl. AI-based biomarkers and surrogate endpoints - Collaborate with clinical operations to integrate imaging AI solutions into trial protocols and workflows - Partner with regulatory teams to ensure imaging biomarkers and AI models meet FDA standards for clinical trial endpoints - Build scalable infrastructure for processing and analyzing large-scale medical imaging datasets from multi-site clinical trials - Present imaging insights and model performance to executive leadership and external partners About You Required Qualifications - Strong communication skills with proven ability to present complex imaging analytics to diverse stakeholders Preferred Qualifications - Experience with regulatory submissions involving imaging endpoints or AI-based image analysis tools - Experience with multi-modal imaging fusion and analysis (combining MRI, CT, PET data) - Knowledge of clinical trial design and experience with imaging core lab operations - Experience with federated learning or privacy-preserving techniques for medical imaging - Understanding of radiomics and quantitative imaging biomarker development - Experience with 3D image reconstruction and volumetric analysis Total Compensation Range: $177,500 - $232,000 Compensation Individual compensation is determined by several factors, including role scope, geographic location, and skills & experience. jobs.title: Manufacturing Quality Assurance Associate II
jobs.description: Are you passionate about ensuring the highest quality standards in manufacturing processes? We are seeking a dedicated and technically adept Manufacturing Quality Assurance (MQA) Associate II professional to join our team. In this pivotal role, you will provide critical QA support and oversight to ensure compliance with good business practices and all applicable health authority regulations. Please note there are 2 on-site positions available (Sunday-Wednesday, Wednesday-Saturday), which can be a day or swing schedule (4 days x 10 hours) based on business need. The Opportunity: As an MQA Associate II you will leverage your strong technical background to resolve issues and devise innovative solutions, ensuring our Oceanside products consistently meet both customer and regulatory requirements. You will also spearhead process improvements, participate in strategic initiatives, and build productive working relationships within the company. Your responsibilities will include overseeing manufacturing documentation, managing deviations, and ensuring our facilities and operational systems align with approved SOPs and cGMP standards. Additionally, you will: Perform higher-level interactions with multiple Genentech departments to resolve any GMP issues observed during manufacturing processes. Perform batch record and batch report review and approval. Participate in cross-functional team meetings for such events as process improvement and/or operational activities as a QA representative. Provide Quality Assurance support for resolving raw material, in-process material, bulk and final product, environmental, and system issues. Provide QA oversight of deviations, working with deviation owners to ensure all requirements are met for closure. Review final evaluations and written summaries that assess product quality impact consistent with Roche and regulatory standards, recommending material dispositions, and identifying timely corrective actions. Participate in routine/non-routine meetings and projects with groups to communicate and resolve system and quality issues tied to deviations and improvement projects. Support FDA/Regulatory and internal inspection activities, as needed. Write and revise SOPs, including Change Control activities. Assess and approve changes associated with Change Control activities. Who You Are: You possess a Bachelor's degree (Biology or Biochemistry preferred) and a minimum of 4 years of relevant of pharmaceutical industry experience. You have comprehensive knowledge of GMPs, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Quality Systems, and general compliance principles. You have demonstrated understanding of Quality Assurance, Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs), Health Authority Regulations, and Validation principles/practices. You possess strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to resolve conflicts calmly, diplomatically, and tactfully in team settings. You have a demonstrated ability to independently manage and influence multiple projects simultaneously. You are proficient in utilizing computer-based systems. Work Environment/Physical Demands/Safety Considerations: The essential functions of this role will be in an office environment. The essential functions of this role requires gowning in the form of hospital scrubs, bunny suits, gloves, and steel toe boots be worn. Note: No makeup or jewelry may be worn when working in the clean room environment. You may be exposed to hazardous materials and chemicals. You may be required to lift up to 30lbs. Relocation benefits are available for this posting. The expected salary range for this position based on the primary location of California is $67,300 - $124,900 Annual. Actual pay will be determined based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other job-related factors permitted by law. A discretionary annual bonus may be available based on individual and Company performance. This position also qualifies for the benefits detailed at the link provided below. Benefits Genentech is an equal opportunity employer. It is our policy and practice to employ, promote, and otherwise treat any and all employees and applicants on the basis of merit, qualifications, and competence. The company's policy prohibits unlawful discrimination, including but not limited to, discrimination on the basis of Protected Veteran status, individuals with disabilities status, and consistent with all federal, state, or local laws. My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Manufacturing Quality Assurance Associate II opportunity with Genentech / Roche at Genentech / Roche.

Best,
Celina Lin

This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. Position Summary MS&T is a science-driven organization dedicated to building in-depth and comprehensive knowledge of our products and their processes. We work across the entire lifecycle of our Pharmaceutical Products and support the Boudry internal manufacturing site The Validation & Investigations Scientist is supporting the Boudry manufacturing process units by executing investigation and/or validation activities within MS&T using established scientific principles, contributing to product quality, process robustness, and cGxP compliance. Acts in one or more domain among Equipment Qualification, Cleaning validation, Process validation, Robustness and Investigations. More specifically, the Validation & Investigations Scientist partners with other site and MS&T functions to design and execute procedures that guarantee the robustness of manufacturing processes at internal sites. Duties/Responsibilities Validation, Qualification & Robustness Author validation and qualification documentation, including but not limited to plans, protocols, reports, traceability matrices and summary reports, in accordance with approved strategies, procedures and regulatory requirements. These documents may be in relation with equipment qualification, process validation, cleaning validation, continued process verification. The designed approaches must include scientific rationales and acceptance criteria, and be based on quality risk management principles. Execute validation, qualification, or robustness activities across the site, including data collection and data analysis. Support introduction of new products or new technologies on the site, by ensuring associated equipment, systems and processes are qualified, validated and maintained in compliance with local policies, guidelines, and procedures during their lifecycle. Perform the assessment of change controls and maintenance interventions, evaluating potential impact to qualified systems and validated processes. Interface with Engineering, Technical Services, Manufacturing, QC, QA and other stakeholders to support MS&T objectives. jobs.title: Model Operations Lead, AI Gateway
jobs.description: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations: Austin, TX | New York City, NY | San Francisco, CA About AI Gateway AI inference is becoming core infrastructure. Every serious application will need access to many models across many providers, with reliability, observability, security, cost control, and routing built in from the start. AI Gateway is Cloudflare's bet that this layer belongs at the network edge: close to users, close to compute, and simple enough that a developer can adopt it with one API change. Developers using AI Gateway need answers to two questions. Is the model I'm calling working the way you say it does? And which model should I be using at all? You'll lead the models team that answers both. You'll start with model operations. That's the work behind every model in the catalog: provider integrations, capability testing, pricing and metering, capacity, security reviews, docs, health, and deprecations. Sometimes a launch needs to go live within minutes of a lab's announcement. Sometimes the right call is to hold it. Cloudflare is an infrastructure company at heart, so reliability and accuracy come first; speed comes from preparation and automation. Then you'll bring model intelligence online. That means turning what we learn from Gateway traffic into decisions for customers: capability maps, per-task rankings, auto-routing profiles that pick the right model for each request, evals and regression detection, and market intelligence developers can trust. This is a people-management role reporting to the AI Gateway Engineering Manager. You'll hire, develop, and lead the team, and you'll stay hands-on: writing code, building agent-driven workflows, and getting into the details of a failed launch or a suspicious eval SLO. Expect to manage people, projects, model stock, and operations all at once. About the Role Build and lead the models team: Hire, coach, and grow the people who run the catalog today and build its intelligence over time. Give people real ownership, give direct feedback, and grow leads who can run their own areas. Run model launches end-to-end: Scope integrations, coordinate testing and evals, confirm pricing, metering, capacity, and security, and get docs and announcements ready. Prepare day-zero launches in advance so they can ship in minutes. Keep the catalog true: Make sure what we publish (capabilities, limits, versions, prices) matches what developers actually get. Catch silent regressions, such as broken tool calling, truncated streams, quantization changes, or usage and pricing mismatches, before customers do. Build model intelligence: As it comes online, own the evals, capability maps, and per-task rankings behind our auto-routing profiles and model recommendations. Make sure they measure what they claim to, and connect regressions to routing decisions so customers who chose "auto" aren't the ones who discover a problem. Treat the catalog and intelligence as products: Have a point of view on which models belong in the catalog, which routing profiles to ship, and what market intelligence to publish. Base it on usage, quality, reliability, and cost data. Turn what you learn into roadmap input. Run a lightweight operating cadence: Keep one source of truth for what's in flight, who owns it, what's blocked, and what ships next. Keep Engineering, Product, Partnerships, and other stakeholders aligned and informed without status meetings. Automate relentlessly: Turn repeatable steps into scripts, tools, and agent workflows: endpoint validation, eval runs, catalog and pricing reconciliation, regression detection, and provider follow-ups. Manual effort per launch should fall as the catalog grows. Responsibilities Day-Zero & Quality Launches: Ensure new models launch on day zero with tested capabilities, accurate pricing, docs, and a clear call on routing eligibility. Catalog Reliability & Health: Ensure the catalog reflects reality, and proactively identify when a model or provider is underperforming before customers notice. Auto-Routing & Optimization: Deliver auto-routing that measurably beats a fixed model choice on cost or quality for users. Developer Trust & Methodology: Build and maintain trusted rankings and recommendations grounded in solid methodology. Partner & Stakeholder Management: Set clear expectations for providers, while keeping Engineering, Product, Partnerships, and other stakeholders aligned. Team Leadership & Growth: Provide clear ownership and direction so the team knows what's next, who owns it, and how to grow into bigger roles. Operational Scalability: Continually drive down the human effort required for each launch, eval, and routing update through tools and automation. You’ll be joining a small team so will have a broad purview over the different Accounting functions, and will have a specific focus on the Order-to-Cash and Revenue workstream. The company is growing fast so the need to revamp, rebuild, and expand our technology infrastructure will be an unending source of exciting projects. Outside of direct projects this is also a great opportunity to join the team at an early stage and help us define how a best in class business systems team should operate! This is a full time role that can be held from one of our US hubs or remotely in the United States. What you’ll do at Figma: Build and provide ongoing system architecture and design reviews to ensure our Order-to-Cash processes are best in class Identify opportunities for configuration, integration, and process improvements across the Order-to-Cash and Revenue Recognition space Align cross-functional teams on technical requirements and goals with regards to ERP functionalities and activities Design and implement software solutions to increase automation, reduce risk, and create scalability Mentor and guide junior team members, as well as provide input on the team’s recruiting efforts by participating in interviewing and hiring decisions Provide occasional support in expanding and troubleshooting systems outside of the Order-to-Cash space, such as Zip, Expensify, Tesorio, Numeric, and Bank of America CashPro Serve as the subject matter expert on NetSuite ERP and provide end user training and support for our ERP and other ancillary Financial systems We’d love to hear from you if you have: 7+ years experience working with accounting teams in a fast growth environment, ideally with strong NetSuite administration experience, including direct experience leading a major system implementation or rollout A solid understanding of Accounting principles and processes Experience supporting ancillary Accounting systems (TripActions, Zip or Coupa, etc.) A balanced skill set that can wear the hats of a Business Analyst, Project Manager and Technical Systems Analyst A passion for helping teams scale and grow through the use of technology While it’s not required, it’s an added plus if you also have: Consulting experience in systems implementation or integrations Experience supporting Stripe, Avalara, or Tesorio At Figma, one of our values is Grow as you go.
